topics.topic: {'title': "Why do you feel 'guilty' when you are not busy?", 'psychological_effect': 'The Productivity Dysmorphia & Internalized Protestant Work Ethic', 'angle': "Analyzing the common Vietnamese 'hustle culture' where young professionals feel a sense of failure or anxiety during weekends or holidays if they aren't 'doing something productive,' leading to chronic burnout even during rest."}

{'title': "Why do you 'over-apologize' to your boss even when you did nothing wrong?", 'psychological_effect': 'The Appeasement Reflex & Conflict Avoidance Bias', 'angle': "Analyzing the common Vietnamese workplace culture where employees reflexively say 'Em xin lỗi' to avoid perceived confrontation or authority-based anxiety, even when the mistake belongs to the company or the manager, leading to a loss of professional self-worth."}

{'title': "Why do you 'doom-scroll' at 2 AM despite being exhausted?", 'psychological_effect': 'Revenge Bedtime Procrastination & Cognitive Offloading', 'angle': "Analyzing the Vietnamese urban phenomenon where young people, feeling they have no control over their long, draining workdays, 'steal' back time at night by scrolling endlessly, essentially sacrificing their sleep to reclaim a sense of personal autonomy."}

{'title': "Why do you feel a strange urge to 'buy' your parents' love with expensive gifts while living far away?", 'psychological_effect': 'The Guilt-Induced Compensatory Altruism & Emotional Outsourcing', 'angle': "Analyzing the common Vietnamese 'expat' or urban-migrant phenomenon where children working in big cities feel immense pressure to send money or luxury goods back home to 'buy' peace of mind, essentially using material gifts as a substitute for the physical presence and emotional labor they cannot provide due to their busy careers."}

{'title': "Why do you 'ghost' your friends' wedding invites even when you really want to go?", 'psychological_effect': "Social Anxiety of Comparison & The 'Performance' Burden", 'angle': "Analyzing the Vietnamese trend of young people avoiding weddings not because they dislike the couple, but because the event feels like a high-stakes 'social performance' where they fear being judged for their current career status, outfit, or lack of a partner, leading to a defensive withdrawal from social circles."}

{'title': "Why do you 'hoard' unread screenshots and saved posts you will never look at again?", 'psychological_effect': 'The Digital Accumulation Bias & Illusion of Competence', 'angle': "Analyzing the Vietnamese 'digital collector' habit where people constantly save career tips, diet plans, or self-help reels into folders they never open. It explores how this behavior creates a false sense of progress and intelligence, acting as a psychological shield against the anxiety of actually having to execute those tasks in real life."}

{'title': "Why do you 'aggressively' organize your desk but never actually start the work?", 'psychological_effect': 'Procrastinatory Displacement & The Planning Fallacy', 'angle': "Analyzing the common Vietnamese office habit of spending the first hour of the morning meticulously cleaning the screen, rearranging files, and organizing icons while avoiding the actual high-pressure task. It explores how 'productive procrastination' serves as a psychological defense mechanism to reduce the anxiety of starting a difficult project."}

{'title': "Why do you 'cringe' at your own past social media posts from 5 years ago?", 'psychological_effect': 'The Spotlight Effect & Retrospective Identity Discontinuity', 'angle': "Analyzing the Vietnamese 'digital footprint' shame. It explores why young adults feel a visceral, physical discomfort when looking at their old Facebook statuses or photos, viewing their past selves as 'strangers' rather than growth, and how this leads to the modern habit of 'purging' or archiving one's entire digital history to curate a more 'sophisticated' current persona."}

{'title': "Why do you feel 'anxious' when your boss sends a message without any context?", 'psychological_effect': 'Ambiguity Intolerance & The Anticipatory Threat Response', 'angle': "Analyzing the 'ping-phobia' in the Vietnamese workplace, where a simple notification like 'Em ơi' or 'Rảnh không?' triggers an immediate fight-or-flight response. It explores how the lack of clear boundaries and the power distance in Vietnamese corporate culture turn a simple digital message into a source of chronic psychological stress."}

{'title': "Why do you 'aggressively' nod and agree in meetings while secretly hating the idea?", 'psychological_effect': 'The False Consensus Effect & Social Conformity Pressure (Asch Conformity)', 'angle': "Analyzing the 'Dạ, vâng' culture in Vietnamese offices. It explores the psychological cost of maintaining a facade of total agreement to avoid being labeled 'difficult' or 'uncooperative,' and how this creates a toxic internal environment where employees feel silenced and resentful despite appearing perfectly aligned with leadership."}

{'title': "Why do you feel an intense 'need' to hide your actual salary from your closest colleagues?", 'psychological_effect': 'The Relative Deprivation Theory & Social Comparison Anxiety', 'angle': "Analyzing the 'salary secrecy' culture in Vietnamese offices. It explores the psychological tension of working side-by-side with peers while viewing them as competitors for status. This behavior turns compensation into a measure of personal worth, leading to a culture of suspicion where transparency is feared as a threat to one's social standing."}

{'title': "Why do you feel a sudden 'urge' to clean your entire house the moment you have a deadline?", 'psychological_effect': 'Productive Procrastination & Anxiety-Induced Displacement', 'angle': "Analyzing the Vietnamese 'Spring Cleaning' phenomenon triggered by work stress. It explores why, when faced with an overwhelming report or project, the brain redirects focus toward low-stakes, physical tasks like scrubbing the floor or rearranging the bookshelf to regain a sense of 'controllable' order amidst emotional chaos."}

{'title': "Why do you 'aggressively' mute your family group chat but check it every 10 minutes?", 'psychological_effect': 'The Paradox of Hyper-Connected Isolation & Boundary Ambivalence', 'angle': "Analyzing the Vietnamese 'family group chat' culture where adult children feel an intense, guilt-driven obligation to stay connected to extended family updates, yet simultaneously feel drained by the constant noise, leading to a cycle of 'digital avoidance' followed by 'anxious checking' to ensure they aren't missing critical family news."}
